neet_phy_u20_t10_1.working: The ammeter must carry the same current as the wire, so it goes in series. The voltmeter measures the potential difference across the wire, so it goes in parallel.

neet_phy_u20_t10_3.working: The slope of the V-I graph is R. For a metal wire, resistance rises with temperature, so at higher currents the slope increases.

neet_phy_u20_t10_4.working: The current is kept small to avoid heating the wire. Heating would raise the resistance and spoil the linear V-I relation. So R correctly explains A.

neet_phy_u20_t10_5.working: R = ρL/A, so doubling L doubles R, which is the slope. Resistivity is a property of the material and stays unchanged, so I is correct. An ideal ammeter has zero resistance and an ideal voltmeter has infinite resistance, so II is correct.
